title: Loops with for and range
lesson:
`for` goes through things one at a time:

```
for crop in ["maize", "beans", "kale"]:
    print(crop)
```

and `range` makes number sequences: `range(5)` is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (five numbers, starting at 0); `range(1, 6)` is 1 to 5; `range(0, 20, 5)` is 0, 5, 10, 15 (step 5). `for i in range(10):` repeats something exactly 10 times.

A for loop over a string goes letter by letter. Loops can go inside loops (**nested**): the inner one runs completely for every round of the outer one, which is how you make tables and grids.

Use `for` when you know what you're going through (a list, a range, a word); use `while` when you repeat until something happens.

notes: Letter by letter; end=" " stays on one line.
A small times table: a loop inside a loop.

exercises.title: Times table
exercises.prompt: Ask for a number and print its times table from 1 to 12, like: 7 x 3 = 21

exercises.title: Count the vowels
exercises.prompt: Write count_vowels(text): how many a, e, i, o, u it has (capitals count too).
hints: Loop over text.lower() letter by letter.

exercises.title: A triangle
exercises.prompt: Write triangle(n) that returns (not prints) a string with n lines: line 1 has one *, line 2 has two, up to n, joined by newlines. triangle(3) is "*\n**\n***".
hints: for i in range(1, n + 1): lines.append("*" * i)

cards.a: The inner loop runs fully for every round of the outer one.

bridge: `for i in range(1, 13):` counts 1 to 12; `for crop in crops:` goes through items (like for-each / for…of).
explain: Explain loops with for and range to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up (not one from the lesson).
